verdictWhy: It vamps, counts a section and leaves the vamp at the end of the pass, track and click together, so the thing that matters works. But the clicks came in sitting on the house bus at -inf instead of on 3 and 4, and I only caught it by digging to the bottom of the Audio tab. I'd run the backup on it once I've checked every click's outputs by hand and rebuilt the keys patch change.

tasks.notes: The import came in with a clear summary. But the click routing was not brought across, the summary described it wrongly, and the keys patch change became a Memo without its program number.

The clicks came in on the Effects bus (outputs 1-2) at -inf, even though the summary said 'outputs of its own'. I fixed it with Own outputs > 3-4 and Level 0 on all three clicks; multi-select made two of them one edit. With 'On its bus' off it doesn't reach the house pair.
The 0:16-0:24 slice came in as an endless loop region. Track and click went round in step. GO on 11 Devamp mid-pass played to 0:24 and went on, tested twice.

The Finale's Slice 1 plays 4 times by itself ('pass 2 of 4 of a counted section'), then holds Slice 2. The bows vamp came in as 0:20-0:30, where the MD says 0:30-0:38. I couldn't tell whether that is the QLab file or the import.
Cmd+T as in QLab. '25' means 0:25 and the time is remembered. To go again: click the Ballad row, Cmd+T, Enter, Space, so four presses. Track and click both start at 0:25.
I selected 30 to 33 and pressed Cmd+R with Start at 300. It numbered all six, children included, 300-305, and the Devamp and Fade targets followed.
Double-clicking '-6' and typing -9 was silently ignored, twice. Click, Cmd+A, -9 worked and the playing track dropped at once. Save then kept it.

Esc fades over 2 s and a second Esc stops dead. Clicking the number's group row puts it back on standby, in Show mode too. Reset is two presses while something plays, and I missed the confirm the first time.

findings.title: Click routing to outputs 3-4 is not imported; clicks land on a house bus at -inf
findings.expected: The QLab workspace sends the clicks to outputs 3 and 4 only. I expected them to come across on 3-4, or at least to be on outputs of their own as the import summary says.
findings.happened: The summary says the clicks are 'played only on outputs of its own, with its main level down'. Opening click's Audio tab shows 'On its bus' lit and 'On its bus's pair.', an empty output matrix, Level '-inf' and Bus 'Effects', which is outputs 1-2. Raising the level, as the summary says to, would put the click in the house.
findings.steps: Import Songbook.qlab5, select 'Opening click', Audio tab, More, scroll to Own outputs.
findings.suggestion: Carry QLab's output routing across, or say plainly that the clicks are now on a house bus.

findings.title: A MIDI program change is imported as a Memo described as 'MIDI timecode, or an empty SysEx', and its program number is lost
findings.expected: A keys patch change is a plain program change, which the app's own MIDI cue sends ('pc 3 ch 2' is its placeholder). It should come across as a MIDI cue.
findings.happened: '21 Keys 2 patch change: was a MIDI cue whose message this does not send (MIDI timecode, or an empty SysEx): kept as a Memo.' The memo's notes do not keep the program number or the channel, so I can't rebuild it without opening the QLab file.
findings.steps: Import Songbook.qlab5 and read the summary, then select 21 and read Notes.
findings.suggestion: Import program changes, and when a cue is turned into a Memo, keep its message in the notes.

findings.title: Double-clicking a negative level and typing a new one is silently ignored
findings.expected: Double-click selects the value and typing replaces it, as in QLab's fields.
findings.happened: Level showed '-6'. I double-clicked, typed -9 and pressed Enter, and it stayed '-6' with no message. It did the same from -9 to -10. I think the double-click selects only the digits, leaving '--9'. Click, Cmd+A, type works.
findings.steps: Select Ballad track, Audio tab, double-click the Level field showing -6, type -9, press Enter. It still shows -6.
findings.suggestion: Select the whole number on double-click, or say when an entry is refused.

findings.title: The cue list scrolls by itself after GO and a click lands on the wrong cue, moving the standby
findings.expected: The row I aimed at a moment ago would still be under the mouse.
findings.happened: I pressed GO on 20 Ballad and then clicked where 'Ballad track' was. The list had scrolled, the click hit '22 Reverb return up', and standby moved to 22.
findings.steps: Scroll so the Ballad group is mid-list, GO it, then click where Ballad track was within a second.
findings.suggestion: Don't scroll under the pointer right after GO.

findings.title: The Finale bows vamp is 0:20-0:30 here, while the MD's notes say 0:30-0:38
findings.happened: Loop regions show 'Slice 1 · 0:00.00 – 0:20.00' (4) and 'Slice 2 · 0:20.00 – 0:30.00' (∞), with markers at 0:20 and 0:30. I can't tell if the workspace was like that or the slices were shifted on import.
findings.steps: Import, select Finale track, Time & Loops, Loop regions.

findings.title: Output routing is buried at the bottom of the Audio tab under More
findings.expected: Output routing at the front, as QLab's Audio Levels tab has it.
findings.happened: Own outputs is under 'More (11)', below fade shapes and Rate, and you have to scroll the inspector twice to reach it.
findings.steps: Select any Audio cue, Audio tab, More, scroll down.

findings.title: Reset's 'Sure?' confirm is easy to miss
findings.expected: Reset to do what its tooltip says, 'Stop all, back to the top', or to make the confirm obvious.
findings.happened: The first press only changed the label to 'Sure? Reset'. I didn't notice and pressed GO, which fired the next cue. It was my mistake, but it is easy to make under pressure.
findings.steps: GO the Opening, press Reset once, look at the standby.

findings.title: Vamp and devamp leave at the end of the pass, with track and click in step
findings.happened: The slice came in as an endless loop region. The click looped with the track. GO on the Devamp mid-pass played to 0:24 and went straight on.

findings.title: Counted section shows which pass it is on
findings.happened: 'pass 2 of 4 of a counted section', then on by itself into the held vamp, with a yellow HOLDING and a Let go button.

findings.title: Load to Time is Cmd+T, remembers the time and says 'LOADED TO 0:25.0 · this GO only'
findings.happened: Same key, '25' read as 0:25, and the next time the field already holds 0:25.

findings.title: Import summary up front, and unsaved changes listed on the Save button
findings.expected: Finding out what broke during a run.
findings.happened: The import sheet lists every cue that changed and says 'The QLab file is unchanged.' The Save button shows 'Save · 3' with the changes in its hint.

rig: The output device is the MacBook speakers, but the test run pretends eight outputs, so I could not see whether a 2-output device would warn about clicks routed to 3-4.
hear does not say which outputs a sound is on, so 'never reaches the house' was checked only from the inspector's routing, not from what came out.
The Reset confirm timed out between my look and my click (the rig's delay between commands).
